identity.retryPolicy: Transport failures (timeout (180s), network error, HTTP 408/409/429/5xx, unreadable API response with 5xx, incomplete or missing output) are retried up to 4 attempts per turn with exponential backoff honoring Retry-After and provider reset headers. Live calls use a 5-second minimum pace, increasing automatically to stay under 80% of a reported token/minute limit, and live episodes cool down by 30 seconds; every attempt and sanitized rate-limit header is recorded. Exhausted HTTP 429 retries interrupt the batch as infrastructure rather than counting as model failure. Invalid model output (unparseable JSON, schema violation, refusal) is not retried or repaired: it is recorded as an invalid response and terminates the episode as unsolved. A valid direction that is visibly blocked is not retried or repaired: it is executed as a blocked move, counts as a wall hit, consumes the turn, and the episode continues.

aiTransport.policy: Provider requests use the shared Vercel AI SDK transport with structured output. SDK retries are disabled; Echo Maze owns every retry, pacing delay, and attempt record.

identity.coordinateSystem: Walker-relative coordinates start at (0,0). A successful move right changes x by +1, left by -1, up by +1, down by -1. A blocked move changes nothing. The Walker never receives absolute maze rows/columns.
identity.hiddenStatePolicy: The prompt receives only the narrow observation DTO (open/blocked directions, corridor sightlines, per-visible-cell open directions and isExit flag, last action/result) plus the current run's conversation. No full maze, no exit coordinates, no seed, no optimal route, no unseen cells, and no spectator state may enter the prompt.

payload.notes: Start (0,0). Moved up into a vertical corridor; continue upward toward the junction seen two cells ahead.
At (0,2), vertical corridor. The next cell upward is a junction with side branches; continue up to reach and inspect it.
At junction (0,3) after moving up. Use systematic exploration: take the long right corridor first; maintain position estimate and inspect the next junction.
At (1,3) in the long horizontal corridor from the junction. Continue right toward the endpoint junction at approximately (5,3), then inspect its branches.
At (2,3), continuing right along the long horizontal corridor toward its endpoint junction near (5,3).
At (3,3), continue right to the endpoint junction two cells ahead, then explore its downward branch before backtracking.
At (4,3), continue right to the endpoint junction at (5,3). The visible endpoint cell has a downward branch; inspect it next.
At the endpoint junction (5,3). The rightward route is blocked and the downward branch is unexplored; descend to inspect it.
At (5,4), the downward branch led to a cell with an unexplored left passage and the return path up. Explore left next.
At (4,4), a dead-end cell with only the right passage open. Backtrack right to (5,4), then continue exploring the remaining route.
At (5,4), the left branch was a dead end and right returned here. Move up to (5,3), then backtrack west along the corridor to explore the remaining branches at the central junction.
At (5,3), the downward branch is fully explored and dead-ended. Backtrack west along the horizontal corridor toward the central junction at (0,3) to inspect the remaining left and downward routes.
Backtracking west along the horizontal corridor toward the central junction at (0,3); the endpoint branch was explored and dead-ended.

At (3,3), continue west along the explored horizontal corridor toward the central junction at (0,3). The eastern branch is exhausted; inspect the central junction's remaining routes after reaching it.
Continuing west toward the central junction. The eastern corridor and its downward branch are exhausted; proceed left until reaching the junction, then inspect remaining branches.
At (1,3), continue west to the central junction at (0,3). The eastern corridor and its downward branch are exhausted; inspect the junction's remaining left and downward routes next.
At central junction (0,3). Eastern route and its branch are exhausted. Explore the remaining western corridor first; the visible endpoint has a downward branch to investigate.
At (-1,3) in the western corridor. Continue left to the endpoint junction at approximately (-2,3), then inspect its downward branch.
At the western endpoint junction (-2,3). The left move reached the junction; inspect its unexplored downward branch next.
At (-2,2) after descending from the western endpoint. The downward branch continues rightward, while up returns to the endpoint; explore right.
At (-1,2), the left route returns to the explored western branch. The downward corridor is unexplored and extends four cells to an endpoint junction; continue down to investigate it.
At (-1,0) in the unexplored downward corridor. Continue down toward the endpoint junction, recording the branch structure before backtracking.
At (-1,-1) in the downward corridor. Continue down toward the endpoint and inspect its left branch.
At (-1,-2) after continuing down the unexplored corridor. Inspect the endpoint's right branch next; backtrack upward if it dead-ends.
At (-1,-2), continue down to the endpoint cell. The right branch is visible from the endpoint and should be inspected next; backtrack up if it is a dead end.
At (-1,-3), the downward move was blocked; the unexplored route is right. Move right to inspect the adjacent endpoint cell, then backtrack if it is a dead end.
At the right-branch endpoint cell. The upward cell is a dead end (only returns down), so backtrack left to the main vertical corridor and then explore remaining routes upward.
At (-1,-2), the right endpoint branch has been checked and is a dead end. Backtrack upward along the main corridor toward the junction at (-1,0) to inspect the remaining rightward route.
At (-1,-1), continuing upward toward junction (-1,0). The lower right branch is exhausted; inspect the junction's remaining rightward route next.
At (-1,0), the lower corridor and its right endpoint branch are exhausted. Inspect the unexplored rightward route from this junction next.
At (-1,1) after moving up from the lower junction. The upward cell has a left branch, while the downward corridor is explored; move up to inspect that remaining branch.
At (-1,1), the upward route ends here and the remaining unexplored passage is left. Move left to inspect the branch; record any new junction or exit.
At (-2,1), both left and down are blocked; this side cell is a dead end. Move right back to (-1,1), then reassess the explored junctions for any missed route.
Returned from the dead-end at (-2,1). The left branch is exhausted; move down along the explored corridor toward the central junction and continue systematic backtracking.
At the lower corridor cell after returning from the dead-end branch. The downward route is exhausted; backtrack upward toward the central junction and reassess unexplored connections.
At (-1,1); left branch is a confirmed dead end and the lower corridor was explored. Backtrack down toward the central junction to continue checking the maze systematically.
At (-1,0); both the lower corridor and its side branch are explored. Retrace upward through the vertical corridor toward the western junction and continue systematic search for the exit.
At the side junction with only the explored downward corridor and a confirmed dead-end left branch. Return down to the lower junction, then retrace toward the central maze area.
At the vertical corridor junction. The lower route and left side branch are explored dead ends; move upward to revisit the upper junction and search for any remaining connection.

At the upper side junction; downward corridor has been traversed, but recheck the left branch before backtracking. The left cell previously appeared dead-ended, so return right afterward and continue systematic exploration.
At (-2,1), the current cell has unexplored upward and rightward passages. Move up first to inspect the branch ahead and update the route map.

At (-2,2) after exploring the upward branch from (-2,1). The downward route returns to the explored western junction, while right leads through the previously mapped corridor; take right to continue checking connectivity.
At (-1,2), the left branch is explored and the rightward corridor leads back toward the central junction. Continue right to inspect the next cell and seek any unvisited route.
At the junction reached by moving right from the western upper corridor. Right and left corridors are mapped; revisit the downward branch to search for any missed exit or connection.

At the vertical corridor below the central junction. The upward junction and its branches are extensively explored; continue downward to inspect the remaining corridor and avoid repeating the mapped upper routes.
At (0,1), the downward cell is a confirmed dead end with only an upward return. Move up to the junction at (0,2) and continue systematic exploration of remaining routes.
At (0,2); the downward cell is a dead end. Move up to the junction at (0,3), where all visible branches have been traversed, and reassess for any overlooked route or exit.
At the central junction; all branches appear mapped without an exit, so re-traverse the eastern corridor systematically and inspect for any newly revealed exit or state change.
At (1,3) in the eastern horizontal corridor. Continue right toward the endpoint junction; the eastern branch was previously explored, but recheck it systematically for the exit.
At (2,3), continuing east through the mapped horizontal corridor. Recheck the endpoint junction and its downward branch for any exit.
At (3,3) in the eastern corridor. Continue right to the endpoint junction; its downward branch was previously checked but should be revisited while searching for the exit.
At (4,3), continue right to the eastern endpoint junction at (5,3). Then inspect its downward branch again for the exit.
At the eastern endpoint junction. The straight corridor is exhausted; descend again into the only remaining branch and inspect the resulting cell for an exit or new passage.
At the eastern branch cell; the left passage is a confirmed dead end. Return up to the eastern endpoint, then continue systematic backtracking toward unexplored possibilities.
At the eastern branch cell. Its left passage is confirmed dead end, so return up to the endpoint junction and continue backtracking west along the main corridor.
At the eastern endpoint junction; the attempted upward move was blocked. The downward branch is exhausted, so backtrack west along the main corridor toward the central junction.
At (4,3) after leaving the eastern endpoint. Continue west along the main horizontal corridor toward the central junction; eastern branches are exhausted.
At (3,3) on the main horizontal corridor, moving west toward the central junction. Eastern corridor and its downward branch are exhausted; continue backtracking to reassess remaining routes.
At (3,3) on the explored horizontal corridor. Continue west toward the central junction at (0,3) to investigate any remaining route; eastern branches are exhausted.
At (1,3), continue west to the central junction at (0,3). The eastern corridor and branches are exhausted; reassess the central and western routes for any remaining exit.

At the central junction after moving west from (1,3). Eastern routes are exhausted; continue systematic exploration from the junction, prioritizing the western branch before revisiting lower corridors.
At (-1,3) in the western corridor. The rightward central route is exhausted; continue left to the western endpoint and recheck its downward branch for the exit.
At western endpoint (-2,3). Move down into its branch again; all other known corridors are exhausted, so continue checking this remaining route for the exit.
At (-2,2) on the western branch. The upward route returns to the endpoint and the right route leads into the mapped corridor; continue right to pursue the remaining path and check for the exit.
At (-1,2); both visible routes are mapped. Move down along the corridor toward (-1,0) and continue systematic backtracking, watching for any exit reveal.
At (-1,0), continue down into (-1,-1). The rightward route from that junction was previously visible but never fully explored; inspect it next for the exit.
At (-1,-1), take the previously unexplored rightward route. Continue mapping this corridor and inspect any junction or exit revealed.
At (0,-1) after entering the previously unexplored rightward corridor. Continue right along this corridor toward its endpoint, checking each junction for the exit.
At (1,-1) in the newly explored horizontal corridor. The route continues right with a junction visible two cells ahead; proceed right to map it and search for the exit.
At (2,-1) in the newly explored corridor. The rightward cell is one step ahead and appears to be an endpoint or junction; continue right to inspect it for the exit or new branches.
At the endpoint of the newly explored corridor; only the left return path is open. Backtrack left through the corridor to revisit the preceding junction and inspect its remaining upward branches.

At (2,-1), backtracked from the dead-end at (3,-1). The unexplored upward branch is one step ahead and leads to a cell with only a downward return; inspect it now before checking the remaining corridor branches.
At (2,0), the upward branch is blocked and the cell only connects downward to the previously mapped corridor. Move down to return to (2,-1), then inspect the remaining unexplored branches there.
At (2,-1), the right endpoint and upward branch are dead ends. Move left back through the newly explored corridor toward (1,-1) and the remaining junction routes.
At (1,-1); the right endpoint and upward branch are dead ends. Continue left through the explored corridor toward the junction at (-1,-1), then reassess remaining branches.
At (0,-1) after backtracking from the explored right-side dead end. Continue left to the junction at (-1,-1), then reassess all connected branches for any missed route or exit.
At the junction (-1,-1). The rightward corridor and its branches are mapped dead ends; lower route is also exhausted. Return upward toward (-1,0) and continue systematic backtracking for the exit.
At (-1,0) after moving up from the lower junction. The downward corridor and rightward branch are exhausted; continue upward to revisit the upper western junction and verify its remaining side route.
At (-1,1) after moving up from (-1,0). Up is blocked and the left branch is a confirmed dead end; move down to return to (-1,0) and continue systematic exploration.
At (-1,0); upper side branch is exhausted. Continue down into the lower junction, then systematically revisit the remaining connected corridor while watching for an exit reveal.
At the lower junction; the right and downward branches are mapped and contain no exit. Move up to return toward the central corridor and continue systematic traversal.
At the vertical corridor cell after moving up from the lower junction. The upper side branch is explored and dead-ends; descend to the junction and continue systematic traversal.
At (-1,-1), right and down branches are fully explored dead ends; only the upward route remains. Move up to (-1,0) and continue systematic traversal.
At (-1,0), move up to recheck the upper side cell and its left branch; the lower corridor and rightward routes have been exhaustively explored.
At (-1,1). The left branch is confirmed dead end, so backtrack down to (-1,0) and continue systematic traversal from the vertical corridor.
At the vertical corridor cell. The upper side branch is a confirmed dead end; continue downward toward the lower junction and recheck its remaining connections.

At the junction after moving down from (-1,0). Up returns through the vertical corridor; right and down branches were previously explored without finding the exit. Recheck the rightward corridor for any state-dependent reveal.
Moved right from the lower junction into the horizontal corridor. Continue right to recheck the remaining corridor and its junctions for a hidden exit.
At (1,-1) after moving right. The upward corridor is unexplored and extends two cells to a junction, while the right branch is mapped. Move up to investigate the new route.
Moved up into the vertical corridor from the newly explored lower-right route. Continue upward to inspect the junction ahead and search for the exit.
At the newly reached upper junction after moving up from (1,1). Up and left are blocked; the right corridor and downward return are open. Explore right, the remaining unvisited direction.
At (2,2) after moving right from the upper junction. The rightward cell is an endpoint candidate with a downward branch; continue right to inspect it for the exit or new passage.
At the endpoint candidate east of the upper junction. The rightward move reached a cell with only left and down open; descend to inspect the remaining branch for the exit.
At (3,1) after descending from the upper-right endpoint. Up returns to the explored branch; the right corridor is newly available and extends two cells, so explore right for the exit.
At (4,1) after moving right from the newly explored branch. The rightward cell is open and appears to lead to an endpoint with a downward branch; continue right to inspect it for the exit.
At (4,1), continue right into the visible endpoint candidate. Inspect its downward branch for the exit or any new passage.
At (5,1) after the blocked right move. The unexplored open direction is down; descend to inspect the endpoint branch for the exit, keeping left as the return route.
At (5,2) after descending from the eastern upper corridor. Down is blocked; up returns to (5,1), while left leads to the remaining unexplored branch. Move left to inspect it for the exit.
At (4,2) after moving left from (5,2). Right returns to the eastern branch; down is the only unexplored open direction. Descend to inspect it for the exit.
At (4,1). The right branch through (5,1)-(5,2) has been explored without an exit. Move up to (4,2), then continue back through the upper junction to inspect any remaining route.
At (4,2), the right branch appears mapped and returns to the eastern corridor. The downward passage is the remaining unexplored direction; descend to inspect it for the exit.
At the lower cell of the upper-right branch after moving down. The right passage leads into the explored eastern loop; move up to return to the junction and continue systematic exploration.

At (4,2) after returning upward. Both available routes are mapped: right returns through (5,2), while down returns to (4,1). Revisit the right branch and continue systematic traversal for any exit reveal.
At (5,2); both up and left routes are mapped, with no exit visible. Backtrack left through the upper-right corridor toward the junction to continue systematic exploration.

At (4,2); right returns to the explored eastern branch, and down returns to the explored upper-right corridor. Continue down to retrace toward the junction and search for any state-dependent exit reveal.

At (4,1) after descending from (4,2). The right branch through (5,1)-(5,2) is explored and has no exit; move up to (4,2), then backtrack west toward the upper junction to inspect remaining connections.
At (4,2); right and down routes are mapped. Descend to (4,1), then retrace west through the upper-right corridor toward the junction at (1,2) to inspect remaining connections.
At (4,1) after descending from (4,2). The right branch through (5,1)-(5,2) is exhausted; move up to (4,2), then retrace west toward the upper junction and inspect remaining connections.

At the upper-right branch cell. Right leads through the explored eastern loop, while down returns toward the lower cell and the route back toward the upper junction. Descend to continue backtracking and search for remaining connections.
At (4,1) after descending from the upper-right branch. The eastern loop is exhausted; move up to (4,2), then backtrack west toward the upper junction to inspect remaining connections.

At the upper-right branch after moving up from (4,1). Left and up are blocked; down returns to the explored lower cell. Take the only remaining route right to inspect the adjacent branch and continue searching for the exit.
At (5,2) after moving right from (4,2). The cell has only up and left open; the eastern branch is fully explored, so move left back toward the upper junction and continue systematic search.
At the upper-right branch cell after returning from (5,2). The right/eastern loop is exhausted; descend to (4,1), then continue retracing toward the upper junction to find any remaining route.

At the lower cell of the upper-right branch. Down and left are blocked; right leads into the exhausted eastern loop. Move up to return to the branch junction and continue backtracking toward unexplored areas.
At (4,2); right leads to the exhausted eastern branch, while down returns to (4,1). Backtrack down toward the upper junction and continue searching for any overlooked connection.
At (4,1) after descending from the upper-right branch. The rightward eastern loop is exhausted; move up to (4,2) and continue backtracking toward the upper junction.

At (4,2); the downward route returns to the explored lower branch, while right leads to the previously explored eastern cell. Take right to exit this loop, then backtrack toward the upper junction and seek any overlooked connection.
At (5,2) after entering the exhausted eastern branch. Only up and left are open; move left to return toward the upper junction and continue systematic backtracking.
At the upper-right loop cell. The eastern branch is exhausted; descend to the connected lower cell, then seek the route back toward the upper junction rather than repeating the rightward loop.

At (4,1) after descending from the upper-right loop. Down and left are blocked; the eastern branch is exhausted. Move up to (4,2) to backtrack toward the upper junction rather than repeating the loop.
